models.name: Model A: 3D FSI CFD Tubing Segment
models.what_it_computes: Transient internal flow and pressure fields in a flexible polymer tube driven by pump pulsation, with fluid–structure interaction resolving wall deformation, lumen collapse progression, shear, and pressure-wave propagation near inline sensors.

models.name: Model B: 1D Network Hydraulic with Axisymmetric Losses
models.what_it_computes: Reduced-order unsteady pressure–flow dynamics across the reservoir, pump cassette, tubing, fittings, and check valves using 1D conservation laws, distributed compliance, and calibrated minor-loss coefficients to predict occlusion-induced transients and detection signals.

mechanisms.name: Downstream Occlusion (Outlet Blockage/Kink)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Outlet blockage increases line pressure and stored elastic volume, delaying alarm and causing unintended bolus release upon clearance; accurate prediction supports safe detection thresholds.

mechanisms.name: Upstream Occlusion (Inlet Pinch/Empty Source)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Inlet blockage induces vacuum and flow starvation, risking under-infusion and cavitation; models must resolve negative-pressure signatures used by detection algorithms.

mechanisms.name: Progressive Tubing Kink Under Bend
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Partial lumen collapse evolves with bending and pressure cycles, altering wave speed and resistance; early detection relies on subtle changes in pressure slope and pulsatility.

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is scored per model–mechanism pair on a 0–5 Evidence Index (half-step allowed), where 0 indicates no supporting evidence and 5 indicates convergent multi-source evidence with reproducibility.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Given the results presented, the models as configured provide credible support to setting and rationalizing occlusion-detection thresholds across the tested operating envelope.

findings.model: Model A: 3D FSI CFD Tubing Segment
spans: Model inputs were drawn from a combination of vendor documentation, in-house material testing, and bench rig charac-terization For tubing, coupon tests provided stress–strain curves and pressure–diameter relationships used to fit Mooney–Rivlin parameters for the 3D FSI model and segment-wise elastance for the 1D network.

For progressive kink, the tolerance band was exceeded in Model B for the highest bend angles at the coldest, most viscous conditions; Model A largely remained within tolerance, with borderline cases at the highest bend angles.
